question.text: A PM using a CASH-FLOW MATCHING strategy for a Rs. 5 crore annuity payable yearly for 10 years will buy:

answer.text: Ten bonds, each maturing in a different year, with principal+coupon matching each annuity payment
One 10-year bond paying all at maturity
Equity for growth and bonds for income

explanation.text: The Logic: A cash-flow matching (dedication) strategy constructs a bond portfolio whose periodic cash inflows (coupons and principal) line up with each future liability outflow. For a Rs. 5 crore annuity payable annually for 10 years, the natural construction is a ladder of ten bonds, each maturing in a different year, with principal plus coupon sized to fund that year's annuity payment. The Trap: A single 10-year bullet bond leaves the first nine annuity payments unfunded; floating-rate bonds reintroduce reinvestment uncertainty; an equity-plus-bond split adds market risk that defeats the purpose of dedicating the portfolio to known liabilities. Note: The Portfolio Managers (NISM-Series-XXI-B) workbook discusses immunization through zero-coupon bonds or duration-matched portfolios and predictable buy-and-hold cash flows but does not explicitly describe a ten-bond cash-flow matching ladder for an annuity. The construction above reflects general industry/regulatory practice in liability-driven investing.
